plan.line: a BH1750 light sensor module (I2C): measures light in lux (1 to 65535), like a light meter: darkness, room light and daylight. Use it when the idea names a BH1750 or needs real lux values; the photoresistor is simpler for dark/bright. Uses one I2C bus (each I2C part needs its own, so at most 2 I2C parts).

code.pinLine: BH1750 light sensor {ref} on I2C{bus} (SDA {gpio}, SCL {scl}): i2c{n} = I2C({bus}, sda=Pin({g}), scl=Pin({sclG}), freq=400000). It needs no driver: once at the start i2c{n}.writeto(0x23, b"\x10") (continuous high-resolution mode), then wait 180 ms; each reading: data = i2c{n}.readfrom(0x23, 2); lux = (data[0] << 8 | data[1]) / 1.2. It measures a new value about every 120 ms. If 0x23 isn't in i2c{n}.scan(), its address is 0x5C.
